title: Pullback to a geometric fibre is the constant sheaf of the geometric stalk
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. For every scheme $h:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, the inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] of $F$ along the composite $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\xrightarrow{\bar s}S$ is canonically isomorphic to the constant sheaf on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with value the geometric stalk $F_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The isomorphism is natural in $U$, in $F$, and in pullback along every $\Omega$-morphism.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.39.3 (Tag 0A3H, label lemma-sections-upstairs), final paragraph, lines 5052-5067; the geometric-fibre inverse-image identification used before the connected-fibre section calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-sections-stalk-natural] to obtain the natural global-section comparison c and its pulled-section germ formula. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], the constant-sheaf counit is an isomorphism at every sheaf on Spec Omega. The global-section evaluation at Mathlib's chosen terminal object is fully faithful; transport this property along the unique terminal-object isomorphism to the explicit identity etale neighbourhood. Its constant-sheaf adjunction therefore also has invertible counit. Whisker this counit with the inverse-image functor and invert it; compose with c whiskered by the constant-sheaf functor to construct beta.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constant-trivialization-pullback] to beta with P = Spec Omega and E the geometric stalk functor. This supplies alpha, normalization alpha_{P,id} = beta and the displayed generator compatibility for every morphism over P.

proof.text: For a unit-pulled section restricted along a, normalization reduces alpha at the identity to beta. Evaluating the sheafification universal property at the identity neighbourhood proves that the inverse constant-sheaf counit sends each section x to its constant-presheaf generator. Naturality of toSheafify moves c through this generator map, and the germ formula of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-sections-stalk-natural] gives the required equality. The compatibility clause is exactly the clause already obtained in the preceding step.
